2608.20054.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies
2608.20054.paper_summary: Multi-module systems often expose every module to the full input. We test whether restricting evidence visibility changes which solutions gradient-based training discovers. Four-cell societies share one frozen pretrained language model and one low-rank adapter, communicating only through two model-width continuous vectors in a fixed relay. On a prospectively sealed natural-language function-composition task, we train ten matched restricted/global pairs sharing initialization bytes, training order, token layout, parameters, and computation; only the attention mask differs. Restricted societies outperform their globally visible twins by at least 20 points at both depths in 9 of 10 pairs, with median paired advantages of 0.7648 and 0.6050. Cutting communication reduces every restricted society to chance, and the depth-three advantage remains 0.558 on programs whose composite function never appeared in training. Across six audited restricted societies, same-value packet transplants preserve behavior at 0.94-1.00 across all tested interfaces; destructive interventions collapse performance; and counterfactual packets redirect outputs toward the mathematically predicted answer. The sole high-performing global model also requires communication, but its same-value packets are not interchangeable across episodes. Restricted visibility is thus not necessary for composition; under this protocol it substantially increases the probability of a generalizing relay and favors a reusable, value-indexed interface. The complete preregistered battery nevertheless formally fails because restricted-arm median depth-three accuracy is 0.6988, below the 0.70 floor. An earlier qualification cohort likewise yielded 0/10 complete passes: one model met every task-performance gate, but all ten failed ordinary-language preservation, confining the system to explicitly task-gated use.
2608.20054.paper_summary_zh: 多模塊系統通常會將每個模塊暴露於完整的輸入中。我們測試限制證據可見性是否改變基於梯度的訓練所發現的解決方案。四個細胞社會共享一個凍結的預訓練語言模型和一個低秩適配器，僅通過兩個模型寬度的連續向量在固定的中繼中進行通信。在一個前瞻性封閉的自然語言函數組合任務中，我們訓練了十對匹配的限制/全局對，這些對共享初始化字節、訓練順序、標記佈局、參數和計算；只有注意力掩碼有所不同。受限社會在10對中的9對的兩個深度上至少超越它們的全局可見雙胞胎20分，配對優勢的中位數為0.7648和0.6050。切斷通信使每個受限社會的表現降至隨機，而深度三的優勢在合成函數從未出現在訓練中的程序上仍然保持在0.558。在六個審計過的受限社會中，相同值的數據包移植在所有測試接口上保持了0.94-1.00的行為；破壞性干預會崩潰性能；而反事實數據包則將輸出重定向到數學預測的答案。唯一高效的全局模型也需要通信，但其相同值的數據包在不同回合中不可互換。因此，受限可見性對於組合並非必要；在這一協議下，它大大增加了通用中繼的概率，並有利於可重用的、值索引的接口。完整的預註冊電池仍然正式失敗，因為受限臂的中位數深度三準確率為0.6988，低於0.70的底線。早期的資格隊列同樣產生了0/10的完整通過：一個模型滿足了每個任務性能門檻，但所有十個都未能保持普通語言，將系統限制在明確的任務門控使用中。
2608.20054.author: Narcis Marincat et.al.
